field: cell biology / biochemistry core facility (protein quantification)
persona: Dr. Elena Fischer, 3rd-year PhD student in a cell-signaling lab, running a BCA total-protein assay on cell-lysate samples (Vehicle vs two doses of 'Drug-A') to normalize protein loading before Western blots. Plate read on the department core facility's SpectraMax M2e reader, still driven by an old Windows XP PC running SoftMax Pro 5.4.1.
source_style: Legacy plate-reader export via SoftMax Pro 5.4.1 'Export to File', which writes a flat tab-delimited .txt table using the Windows OS default codepage (Windows-1252 / cp1252) rather than UTF-8 -- a known gotcha with pre-2010s Windows-only lab instrument software.

columns.name: Plate ID
columns.notes: Constant across the file; identifies this plate/run.

columns.name: Well
columns.notes: 96-well plate coordinate; only wells A1-D4 used in this partial run.

columns.name: Sample ID
columns.notes: STD-<conc> for the 9 standard-curve calibrators, LYS-<n> for the 11 unknown lysate samples.

columns.name: Treatment Group
columns.notes: 'Standard' for calibrators; Vehicle / Drug-A 1uM / Drug-A 10uM for unknown lysates.

columns.name: Absorbance (562nm)
columns.notes: Raw instrument absorbance reading for the BCA colorimetric reaction.

columns.name: Concentration (µg/mL)
columns.notes: Known nominal concentration for standards; back-calculated protein concentration for unknown samples. Header cell contains U+00B5 MICRO SIGN (0xB5 in cp1252) -- the byte that forces the non-UTF-8 encoding.

columns.name: Dilution Factor
columns.notes: Constant 1 in this run (no pre-dilution applied to any sample).

columns.name: Temp (°C)
columns.notes: Reader chamber temperature at read time. Header cell contains U+00B0 DEGREE SIGN (0xB0 in cp1252), a second byte that forces the non-UTF-8 encoding.

columns.name: Replicate
columns.notes: Technical replicate number within the duplicate well pair for each sample/standard.

columns.name: QC Flag
columns.notes: 'OK', or 'OOR-HIGH' when absorbance exceeds the top standard's reliable range (>1.95).

intended_analysis: Fit a standard curve (linear or 4-parameter logistic) to the absorbance-vs-known-concentration Standard rows, use it to back-calculate protein concentration for each unknown lysate sample, average technical replicates per Sample ID, then compare mean concentration across Treatment Group (Vehicle vs Drug-A 1uM vs Drug-A 10uM) via one-way ANOVA -- the resulting concentrations are used to normalize protein loading for downstream Western blots.
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A naive reader that assumes UTF-8 (Python's open() text-mode default, or a spreadsheet import left on UTF-8) raises UnicodeDecodeError right at the 'Concentration (µg/mL)' header cell, because 0xB5 ('µ' in cp1252) is not a valid UTF-8 leading byte -- the file fails to load at all rather than silently mis-decoding. A reader that gets the encoding right but assumes comma-separated values (a common default for .txt) sees every row collapse into a single garbage column instead of ten. And someone who correctly guesses 'it's not UTF-8' but decodes as latin-1/ISO-8859-1 instead of cp1252 is silently WRONG in general (cp1252 remaps 0x80-0x9F to printable characters that latin-1 leaves as control codes) -- though in this particular file µ=0xB5 and °=0xB0 happen to decode identically under latin-1 and cp1252, so those two header symbols would look correct by coincidence and mask that the wrong codec was used.
